findings.text: the calibration ruler is emitted for a human reader only; nothing in the committed tree reads the position where the pane cut it. The production width is the ancestor terminal's ioctl column count passed through calibrated_width (reckon/crew/ticker.py:367), which equals the ruler's break on a real pty but is not the ruler itself, and a detached follower falls back to DEFAULT_WIDTH with no ruler observation at all. The plan's intent — a width measured rather than a guessed constant — is met, and 'where it is cut recorded' is satisfied by the ioctl reading; stated here so a reader does not assume the emitted ruler is parsed back.

the wall cell blanks on any transition into dispatched regardless of whether spend_wall_seconds carries a real value (test_a_measure_noise_for_the_row_state_renders_blank_not_the_marker renders a dispatched event with 1234.0s and still expects seven blanks), so a re-dispatch whose elapsed figure would be meaningful is blanked too. This is exactly the plan's stated definition — a transition into dispatched is time zero by definition — and the docstring documents it, so it is a design note recorded for the next reader with a different event model, not a defect.

the flush of the cut spend cells leaves tests/test_crew_recovery.py::test_a_resumed_runs_line_carries_measured_values_not_markers broken (AttributeError: module has no attribute MODEL_SECS at tests/test_crew_recovery.py:1720, reproduced at head here), which the manifest correctly reports as a follow_on outside its write scope; under the merged-head attribution run it will fail a wider suite, so the promotion that lands this commit must bundle the repair or the review record that owns it, not treat the four-file gate as the whole story.

justifications.durability: every behaviour the measure names has a failing-flips test in the commit: a re-added INSET or guessed margin fails `assert not hasattr(ticker_module, "INSET")` (test_calibration_consumes_an_observed_cut_position, tests/test_crew_ticker_layout.py), a column re-added to the row fails the reason-floor test, blanking or the marker removed on a dispatched row fails test_a_measure_noise_for_the_row_state_renders_blank_not_the_marker, and a repeated or json-leaked ruler fails test_the_ruler_is_emitted_once_and_only_on_a_human_stream (tests/test_crew_ticker.py).
justifications.evidence: the manifest's arithmetic reproduces independently here: base 101 passed / 0 failed and head 106 passed / 0 failed re-run in the reviewed worktree (/tmp/review_rowrenders_base.log, /tmp/review_rowrenders_head.log), the reason floor measures 76 free columns at the observed 208-column cut against 58 at base (both rendered through the calibration path), and the lint delta reproduces as 4 base vs 3 head real findings with only one strict-zip fixed, none added (see finding).
justifications.fit: ruler_line, calibrated_width and RULER_LENGTH follow the module idiom — a named module constant, a one-paragraph mechanism docstring, and a floor raised like the pre-existing mins — the four naming checks over the diff's added lines find nothing banned, and the comments state the mechanism ('where the pane broke the ruler — a reading, not a guess') rather than the work item.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all three plan measures land and are asserted: the render width is the observed cut with the provisional inset constant deleted (calibrated_width(208)==208, resolve_terminal_width()==208 on a real pty), a cell whose row state makes its figure noise renders blank while the absence marker survives a genuinely unmeasured figure (test_a_measure_noise_for_the_row_state_renders_blank_not_the_marker), and the reason field grows from 58 to 76 columns at the measured pane width on the commit's own fixture (tests/test_crew_ticker_layout.py, '> = 75' assertion).
justifications.scope_discipline: commit b876427 touches exactly four files — reckon/crew/ticker.py, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_crew_ticker.py, tests/test_crew_ticker_layout.py — every one inside the declared seven-path write scope, with no out-of-fence path modified and the three declared but unchanged test files still green at head (tests/test_monitor_invocation_docs.py 4 passed here).
